Subject: Request: subprocessor inventory and cross-border details for DPA amendment

Hi Camila,

We are preparing a small DPA addendum for our integration with Redwood and need a current list of subprocessors plus a short note on where processing occurs for each (EU, US, APAC). Specifically: 1) canonical subprocessor name and role, 2) whether it receives persisted customer data or only ephemeral inference traffic, and 3) whether any cross-border transfers occur that we should list in our export control & transfer clause.

Can you share this by end of week? Also include any planned additions within the next 90 days if available. Our legal team will use this to prepare the DPA amendment (we expect to propose a standard 30-day notice clause).

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
FinFuse

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>

Subject: Subprocessor inventory + processing locations (attached)

Hi Laura / FinFuse Legal —

Please find attached our current subprocessor inventory (CSV) and a short PDF that summarizes processing location and transfer notes. Key points up front to help with the DPA amendment: 

- Inventory includes: EdgeFlow (CDN / edge routing), VaultKey (KMS/HSM for customer-managed keys), NimbusOps (GPU orchestration), EchoLogs (logging & audit retention), ShortCache (prefix caching layer), and AWS (S3 for long-term backups in select regions).

- For each vendor we identify whether they receive persisted customer data (yes/no): EdgeFlow = no (ephemeral only), VaultKey = yes (encrypted keymetadata, customer-controlled), NimbusOps = yes (model weights + ephemeral KV cache; backups encrypted), EchoLogs = yes (audit logs, anonymized PII redaction where applicable), ShortCache = no, AWS = yes (long-term backups, region-specific).

- Cross-border transfer summary: most inference traffic is routed to the nearest region (EU customers keep inference within eu-1 or eu-2 regions by default). Where customers pin to 'global' routing, requests may transit through US endpoints for orchestration, but persisted backups are kept in the customer-chosen region unless otherwise agreed. Our default transfer controls are documented and we can sign the standard DPA export control clause or an appendix with per-account commitments.

- Planned additions (next 90 days): evaluating a second EU logging partner (for higher retention in eu-1), and a multi-region HSM partner for APAC. These are candidates and not yet contractually engaged; we'll provide 30-day notice for any additions as requested in the DPA.

Attachments (referenced inside CSV): subprocessor_inventory_20260318.csv, redwood-dpa-amendment-diff.pdf

If FinFuse needs any of the following called out explicitly in the DPA, let us know: subprocessor roles mapped to data categories (we can add a column), KMS key ownership model, and an explicit clause for ephemeral-only processors.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finfuse.com>

Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory + processing locations (attached)

Thanks Mina — this is exactly what we needed and very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from our legal team before we finalize the DPA addendum: 

1) For EdgeFlow you list "ephemeral only" — can you confirm whether any edge logs (IP/connection metadata) are retained longer than 7 days for debugging? If so, we need that retention window stated.
2) On AWS backups: which specific regions are used when a customer selects EU residency? We need codified assurance that backups for EU-resident accounts will be stored in eu-1 (Frankfurt) or eu-2 (Ireland) only.

If you can add those two clarifications to the CSV or the PDF, we can circulate a draft addendum to our counsel. If easier, our counsel is happy to take the language you suggested in redwood-dpa-amendment-diff.pdf and propose final wording — we can coordinate edits over DocuSign or a shared Drive doc.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
FinFuse
